body.process_wide_state: The service imports one new module, app/inflight_guard.py, whose module-level instance `guard` is a process-wide object (constants MAX_INFLIGHT 26 and QUEUE_WAIT_S 20.0; the asyncio primitives are created lazily inside the running loop, so import creates no semaphore, task or loop), and app/tools.py's _PolicyGuardedMCP.call_tool, the dispatch chokepoint of EVERY tool, now runs the tool body inside `async with inflight_guard.guard.slot(name)` after the entitlement denial (a denied call takes no slot): a call beyond the 26-th concurrent one waits up to 20 s and is then returned as an enveloped gateway_busy refusal, audited as denied/gateway_busy. app/harvest_typed.py's project() (used by every typed tool and the client core) now measures size as json.dumps(indent=2). READ, not instrumented: I opened app/inflight_guard.py whole (76 lines: imports asyncio, contextlib and typing, two constants, the Busy exception, the InflightGuard class and `guard = InflightGuard()`), the OG-mg-3 hunks of app/tools.py (the added import and the try/except around call_tool; no other module-level statement) and the OG-sz-1 hunks of app/harvest_typed.py (the _size measure and project()). No logger, handler, signal, thread, socket, environment read, sys.path change or global-config change happens at import. tools/list does NOT change: the candidate registry counted 103 tools on the host against 103 at the live ref (no tool is added). Nothing arms the probe listener or writes any parameter.
